title: An etale atlas presents an algebraic space as its relation quotient
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $p:h_U\to X$ be a representable surjective etale map from an $S$-scheme $U$. Let $R=U\times_XU$ be the scheme representing this sheaf fibre product [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], with projections $s,t:R\to U$. The map $(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ is an equivalence relation: for each $S$-scheme $T$, it identifies $R(T)$ with the pairs $(a,b)\in U(T)^2$ satisfying $p\circ a=p\circ b$. The projections $s,t$ are surjective etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $Q$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] of the presheaf $T\mapsto U(T)/R(T)$. The canonical map $Q\to X$ induced by $p$ is an isomorphism and identifies the quotient map $h_U\to Q$ with $p$.

source.place: Tag 0262, lemma-space-presentation, clauses (1)-(3); the surjectivity of s,t follows also from their diagonal section.

proof.text: Work on the big fppf site fixed in the statement. The hypothesis on $p$ is a representable map of sheaves, with the meaning of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The scheme $R$ represents $h_U\times_Xh_U$, as supplied by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] to the finite pullback diagram: for every $S$-scheme $T$, $R(T)=\{(a,b)\in U(T)^2:p_T(a)=p_T(b)\}$. The scheme fibre-product property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $(U\times_SU)(T)$ with $U(T)^2$. Thus $(s,t)$ identifies $R(T)$ with this subset. Equality in $X(T)$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so these subsets are equivalence relations, compatible with restriction in $T$. This proves precisely the equivalence-relation assertion.

source.place: Tag 0262 (lemma-space-presentation), first paragraph; sectionwise limits are Sites Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf)

proof.text: Test $p:h_U\to X$ against the scheme map $p:h_U\to X$ itself. By the definition of representable surjective etale in [def-trf-algebraic-space], the resulting projection $U\times_XU\to U$ is a surjective etale scheme morphism. This is one of $s,t$. Interchanging the two factors, by $(a,b)\mapsto(b,a)$ in the preceding description, identifies the other projection with the same base change. Consequently both $s$ and $t$ are surjective etale. This uses the scheme-test definition directly, so no extra separation, finiteness or quasi-compactness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0262 (lemma-space-presentation), second sentence of proof, with surjectivity from the same scheme test

proof.text: Let $T\to S$ be an object of the big fppf site and $\xi\in X(T)$. By [def-trf-algebraic-space], the pullback $V=T\times_{\xi,X,p}U$ is a scheme and $v:V\to T$ is surjective etale. The definition [def-weil-etale-morphism] makes $v$ flat and locally of finite presentation; hence the singleton $\{v:V\to T\}$ is an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site]. The second projection $a:V\to U$ satisfies $p\circ a=\xi|_V$ by the defining pullback equality. Thus every section of $X$ lifts locally to $h_U$. Both $h_U$ and $X$ are the sheaves in the given representable map, so [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] applies and proves that $p$ is an epimorphism in this category of sheaves of sets.

source.place: Tag 0262 (lemma-space-presentation), third paragraph; Topologies Tag 021M (definition-fppf-covering), Sites Tags 00WM/00WN (definition-sheaves-injective-surjective, lemma-mono-epi-sheaves)

proof.text: The sheaf $h_R$ with its two projections is the kernel pair of the epimorphism $p$, by step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-kernel-pair-coequalizer] to $\mathcal P=h_U$, $\mathcal F=X$ and $K=h_R$. Its hypotheses are exactly the sheaf pullback of step 1 and the epimorphism of step 3. It follows that for every sheaf $H$ and map $b:h_U\to H$ with $b\circ s=b\circ t$, there is a unique map $c:X\to H$ with $c\circ p=b$.

source.place: Tag 086K (lemma-coequalizer-surjection), applied as in the last sentence of spaces.tex Tag 0262

proof.text: Write $P(T)=U(T)/R(T)$ and let $q:h_U\to Q=P^\#$ be the quotient map followed by the sheafification unit. Restrictions preserve the relation in step 1, so $P$ is a presheaf. For every sheaf $H$, a map $b:h_U\to H$ equalizing $s,t$ descends uniquely to $P\to H$: on each $T$ send $[a]$ to $b_T(a)$. This is well-defined because $b_T(a)=b_T(a')$ whenever $(a,a')\in R(T)$, and it is natural because $b$ is natural; conversely every map $P\to H$ has this property. By the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], these maps are in bijection with maps $Q\to H$. Therefore $(Q,q)$ has the same coequalizer property as $(X,p)$ in step 4. Taking $H=X$ gives the specified map $\alpha:Q\to X$ with $\alpha q=p$, and taking $H=Q$ in step 4 gives $\beta:X\to Q$ with $\beta p=q$. Now $\alpha\beta p=p$, so uniqueness for $(X,p)$ gives $\alpha\beta=1_X$; likewise $\beta\alpha q=q$, so uniqueness for $(Q,q)$ gives $\beta\alpha=1_Q$. Thus the canonical map $\alpha$ is an isomorphism and its equality $\alpha q=p$ gives the required identification of quotient maps.

source.place: Tag 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), universal property; identifies the presheaf-quotient formulation with the coequalizer of spaces.tex Tag 0262

lean.statement: theorem etale_atlas_presentation {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (U : Over S) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (hp : IsEtale p) (hsur : IsSurjective p) (R : Over S) (s t : R ⟶ U) (hR : IsPullback (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) p p) (Q : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (η : coequalizer (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ⟶ Q.obj) (hη : ∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun a : Q.obj ⟶ G.obj ↦ η ≫ a)) : Mono (prod.lift s t) ∧ (∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ U ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b) ∧ ∀ a b : T ⟶ U, (∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b) ↔ p.app (op T) a = p.app (op T) b) ∧ Etale s.left ∧ Surjective s.left ∧ Etale t.left ∧ Surjective t.left ∧ IsIso (etaleAtlasPresentationMap p s t hR Q η hη) ∧ (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ≫ η) ≫ (etaleAtlasPresentationMap p s t hR Q η hη).hom = p
lean.note: The canonical comparison is constructed by the inverse sheafification hom-set bijection applied to the presheaf coequalizer descent of p. Q and its unit are specified by the universal property at this quotient presheaf, preserving the published small-valued algebraic-space interface on the big fppf site. The representing scheme R is an arbitrary supplied representative, expressed by its Yoneda pullback square.
